questions.stem: In metallic bonding, what happens to the outer electrons of metal atoms?

options.text: They are transferred to non-metal atoms
They are shared in pairs between two atoms
They are destroyed and converted into energy
They become delocalised and free to move throughout the structure

questions.explanation: In metallic bonding, metal atoms lose their outer electrons, which become delocalised (free to move). The positive metal ions are then held together by their attraction to this 'sea' of delocalised electrons.
